goal:
Build an ORDERS feature for this Vite + React 19 + TypeScript store, wired into the existing app. No new runtime dependencies (vitest may be added as a dev dependency). Strict TypeScript, no `any`, JSDoc on every export, `npm run build` must pass and `npx vitest run` must be green.

1. src/orders/types.ts — the domain: `Order`, `OrderLine`, `OrderStatus` ("pending" | "paid" | "shipped" | "delivered" | "cancelled"), `Address`, `PaymentMethod`, `OrderError` (a typed Error subclass with a `code` of "declined" | "out_of_stock" | "network"), and `OrderDraft` (what the UI holds before submission).
2. src/orders/api.ts — a mock backend over a seeded in-memory store: `listOrders()`, `getOrder(id)`, `placeOrder(draft)`, `cancelOrder(id)`, `advanceOrder(id)` (pending→paid→shipped→delivered). Every call returns a Promise resolving after 50–150 ms; `placeOrder` rejects with OrderError("declined") when the card number ends in "0000" and OrderError("out_of_stock") when a line's qty exceeds 10. Ids are `ORD-<8 uppercase base36>`, stable and unique.
3. src/orders/storage.ts — orders persist to localStorage under "ministore:orders" through a versioned envelope, validated on load (drop malformed orders, clamp line quantities to 1..99, unknown status → "pending"), with `loadOrders()`, `saveOrders(orders)` and `clearOrders()`.
4. src/orders/totals.ts — pure money maths over an order: `subtotal(order)`, `shipping(order)` (free over $50, else $7.99), `tax(order, rate)` (rounded to the cent, half-up), `total(order)`, and `formatOrderTotal(order, locale)` via Intl.NumberFormat. All amounts are whole dollars in `Product.price`, as the existing catalogue has them.
5. src/orders/status.ts — the state machine: `canTransition(from, to)`, `nextStatus(current)`, `isTerminal(status)`, `statusLabel(status)` (human wording) and `transitionsFor(status)` (what the UI may offer). Cancelled and delivered are terminal; nothing moves backwards.
6. src/orders/useOrders.ts — the React hook binding the pieces: `orders`, `loading`, `error`, `place(draft)`, `cancel(id)`, `advance(id)`, `refresh()`; it loads from storage on mount, writes through on every change, surfaces OrderError by code, and never leaves `loading` stuck after a rejection.
7. src/orders/OrdersPage.tsx — the screen: a list of orders (id, date, status pill, total, line count), an empty state, a detail panel for the selected order showing its lines and the totals breakdown, and per-order actions driven by `transitionsFor` (Cancel, Advance) with the buttons disabled while a call is in flight.
8. src/orders/OrderRow.tsx — the row component used by the page: props `{ order, selected, onSelect, onCancel, onAdvance, busy }`, keyboard accessible (Enter/Space selects), with the status pill coloured per status.
9. Wire it in: a "Orders" button in the existing header of src/App.tsx toggles between the store page and OrdersPage; placing an order from the existing cart drawer (the Checkout button) creates an order through `useOrders().place` and clears the cart. The store page must keep working exactly as it does now.
10. Tests (vitest, jsdom not required): at least 40 unit tests across api (ids, delays, both rejection paths), storage (round trip, corrupt store, clamping, unknown status), totals (each function, the free-shipping boundary, tax rounding), status (every legal and illegal transition, terminals) and useOrders' pure helpers. `npx vitest run` must be green.
11. README.md — an "Orders" section: the storage key, the status machine, the shipping and tax rules, and how to run the tests.

gates.name: The judge
gates.detail: The nine module tasks were filled with real, well-typed code that broadly matches their acceptance criteria (types, api, storage, totals, status, hook helpers, two components, App wiring), but goal item 11 (README "Orders" section) was never written and was not even represented in the plan, and t9's toggle criterion is not met. More seriously, OrdersPage calls useOrders() independently of App's instance, so two hooks hold separate state over the same localStorage key and over an api module whose in-memory store is not the persisted one — cancel/advance on any order restored from storage reject
